
### Assignment: Computing summary stats for 4 traits broken down by population and region

```{r}
summary((tapply(traits$Survival, traits$Region)), na.rm = TRUE)

summary((tapply(traits$Genetic_Diversity, traits$Population)), na.rm = TRUE)

summary((tapply(traits$Genetic_Diversity, traits$Region)), na.rm = TRUE)

summary((tapply(traits$Germination, traits$Population)), na.rm = TRUE)

summary((tapply(traits$Germination, traits$Region)), na.rm = TRUE)

summary((tapply(traits$Fitness, traits$Population)), na.rm = TRUE)

summary((tapply(traits$Fitness, traits$Region)), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Producing figures

```{r}

#Histogram

#box-plots (per chosen variable, out of curiosity
boxplot(Fitness ~ Region, data = traits, main = "Fitness by Region", ylab = "Fitness", pch = 19)

boxplot(Survival ~ Region, data = traits, main = "Survival by Region", ylab = "Survival", pch = 19)

boxplot(Genetic_Diversity ~ Region, data = traits, main = "Genetic Diversity by Region", ylab = "GenDiverse", pch = 19)

boxplot(Germination ~ Region, data = traits, main = "Germination by Region", ylab = "Germination :)", pch = 19)
```

## Idea-check responses

1.  What is the difference between vector and a
    data-frame in R?
    1.  Vectors are 1 dimensional columns where
        all elements have to be homogeneous #or
        the same type of variable whether its
        numeric or a character. A data-frame is a
        way #to present this information . Each
        column acts as a vector, but they have to
        be #the same size. Data-frames can have
        heterogeneous data, so they can contain
        numbers and characters.
2.  Why prefer a relative path over an absolute
    path?
    1.  This allows others to run your code
        successfully, without having to edit file
        paths or break file links. Absolute paths
        are user-centric whereas relative paths
        can be used by otherss when they run your
        code locally on their device or on a
        shared space such as the cluster.
3.  What does str(traits) tell you that
    head(traits) doesn't?
    1.  str() will show the name of the column(s)
        whereas head() will show what the actual
        file's rows say. It is useful to check
        both in case R misreads the file and shows
        the name of the column incorrectly. This
        can help show if data needs to be
        rearranged within the file itself for R to
        read it properly.
4.  Why does treating Region as a factor matter
    for boxplot(Height \~ Region, data = traits)
    1.  Treating Region as a factor allows the
        function to work, since it requires
        numerical data. I think that keeping
        Region as a character wouldn't be
        compatible with this function.
5.  If mean(traits\$height) returned NA, what
    would you check first & how would you fix it?
    1.  I could review the column to have
        sums(is.na(x)) count the amount of NAs in
        that part of the data. to prevent this
        from interfering with the function again,
        I can add rm.na = TRUE to tell R to ignore
        thesevalues and only work with the ones
        present
